'''''Najas gracillima''''',<ref>Magnus, Paul Wilhelm. 1870.  Beitrage zur Kenntniss der Gattung Najas 23, ''Najas gracillima ''</ref><ref>Engelmann, Georg. 1867. Manual of Botany of the Northern United States (ed. 5) 681, ''Najas indica'' var. ''gracillima''</ref><ref>Tzvelev, Nikolai Nikolaievich. 1979. Novosti Sistematiki Vysshikh Rastenii. Moscow & Leningrad 16: 208, ''Caulinia amurensis''</ref><ref>Nakai, Takenoshin. 1937. Journal of Japanese Botany 8:853, ''Najas japonica''</ref> the '''slender waternymph''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=NAGR|taxon=Najas gracillima|accessdate=16 July 2015}}</ref> is a [[submergent plant|submerged]] species of [[aquatic plant]] in the [[Hydrocharitaceae]] family.<ref name=KewPOWO>{{cite web|url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:603011-1|title= Najas gracillima (A.Braun ex Engelm.) Magnus|author=<!--Not stated-->|date=n.d.|website=Plants of the World Online|publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|access-date= September 26, 2020}}</ref> found in lakes and streams. It is native to [[China]] ([[Fujian]], [[Guangxi]], [[Guizhou]], [[Hainan]], [[Hebei]], [[Hubei]], [[Jiangxi]], [[Jilin]], [[Liaoning]], [[Nei Mongol]], [[Taiwan]], [[Yunnan]], [[Zhejiang]]), [[Russian Far East]] ([[Amur Oblast|Amur]] and [[Khabarovsk]]), [[Japan]], [[Korea]], [[Taiwan]], [[Iran]], [[Alberta]], [[Ontario]], [[Newfoundland]], [[Nova Scotia]], [[New Brunswick]], the eastern [[United States]] (every state east of the [[Mississippi River]] except [[Florida]], plus [[Minnesota]], [[Iowa]], [[Missouri]] and the [[District of Columbia]]). It is also considered introduced and naturalized in [[France]], [[Spain]], [[Italy]] and [[California]] ([[Plumas County, California|Plumas]] and [[Tehama County, California|Tehama Counties]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=308248|title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|website=apps.kew.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-01-31}}</ref><ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Najas%20gracillima.png Biota of North America Project, ''Najas gracillima ''] Image</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=222000256|title=Najas gracillima in Flora of China @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-01-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000256|title=Najas gracillima in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-01-31}}</ref>

''Najas gracillima'' is a small aquatic annual with branching stems. The unisexual flowers ( each flower is only one sex) are produced in the axils of the branchlets and bases of the leaf sheaths.<ref name="CoffinPfannmuller1988">{{cite book|author1=Barbara Coffin|author2=Lee Pfannmuller|title=Minnesota's Endangered Flora and Fauna|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wfWNq91AjeoC|year=1988|publisher=U of Minnesota Press|isbn=978-0-8166-1689-3|page=116}}</ref>  It is listed as endangered in Minnesota.<ref name="CoffinPfannmuller1988"/> It lives in soft-water lakes and ponds with mud and silt bottoms, and appears to be sensitive to water turbidity, warming, and [[eutrophication]].<ref name="CoffinPfannmuller1988"/>
